title: Conjugation outgrowths and root-hairs arise at sites of potassium concentration

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Conjugation outgrowths and root-hairs arise at sites of potassium concentration

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The bulges that begin conjugation in algae such as Pleurocarpus and Mesocarpus, and the root-hair outgrowth of Equisetum spores, arise where surface tension is weakened, and these sites coincide with heavy concentrations of potassium salts, which disperse when the cell becomes symmetrical again.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VI: A Note on Adsorption

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: This bulge is, in the first place, a sign of weakened surface tension on one side of the cell, which as a whole had hitherto been a symmetrical cylinder; in the second place, we see that the bulging area corresponds to the position of a great concentration of the potassic salt

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VI, “A Note on Adsorption”; topic “Potassium concentration and weakened tension”. Scope: conjugating zygnematacean algae, germinating Equisetum spores and other cells forming local outgrowths

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch06-07: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.49

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Temporal precedence and colocalization provide clear criteria. Public morphogenesis movies may resolve shape change, but the paired chemical and mechanical channels needed for the mechanism are not generally available.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In time-lapse images, determine whether potassium enrichment and reduced cortical tension precede conjugation bulges or root-hair emergence and disappear when symmetry returns.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The claim spans unrelated algal and plant systems.

Relevant time series usually lack potassium sensors and tension measurements.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Coincidence of a potassium peak with the conjugation papilla or the spore outgrowth is a concrete spatial prediction. No current public dataset repeats that histochemistry with coordinates and time. The test is straightforward in principle and cannot be run on data that exist today.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Map potassium through conjugation in zygnematacean filaments and through rhizoid outgrowth of Equisetum spores. A potassium peak that precedes the bulge and disperses when symmetry returns would support the claim; outgrowths without a potassium peak, or peaks that persist after the cell is symmetrical, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The spatial potassium records for Pleurocarpus, Mesocarpus and Equisetum spores are essentially early histochemical plates, not reusable measurements.

A spatial coincidence, even if remeasured, would still leave open whether potassium causes the bulge or follows local growth.
